name: Catapult Lot

description: Concept rendering only. Surface lot facing Lake Mirror next to Catapult, Lakeland's startup hub, with the Amtrak station a short walk east along Main Street.
zoning: C-6 Downtown Commercial; Urban Center (UCT) context; Future Land Use RAC; Downtown CRA; not in a local historic district
max_height: 120 ft (~10 stories: 16 ft retail + 9 x 10.5 ft residential); min 24 ft street facade; no LDC height bonus
by_right_sqft: ~215,500 GSF (39,511 sf ground floor + 176 units x 1,000 GSF); FAR 5.0 cap = 219,505 sf. With 75% minimum lot coverage, FAR works out to ~6-7 stories average, or a podium plus a slimmer tower to reach 120 ft
parking: None required: inside Downtown Parking Exempt Area. Lot now provides ~100 spaces used by Catapult; replacement parking is a tenant/business issue. Parking garage = conditional use in C-6.

opportunity_zone: Census tract 12105016400 (tract 164): current 2018 Opportunity Zone, in effect through 12/31/2028, but NOT nominated for OZ 2.0 (new zones start 1/1/2027). Treat OZ as a closing window, not a selling point.
cra: Downtown CRA. Precedents: Peachtree Flats TIF rebate = 75% of City+County increment for 5 yrs after CO, plus up to $775k site/infrastructure reimbursement; Onicx (Oak St, 2022) = 80% yrs 1-5 / 60% yrs 6-10 plus fee help. LDDA Curb Appeal grant (50% match) for storefront items.

Polk County fees collected in Lakeland add roughly $11,016/MF unit incl. $8,055 school fee (third-party compilation, Aug 2026; verify with Polk County). City offers impact-fee financing (4 yrs) for commercial projects with $400k+ water/wastewater fees.
water_sewer: City Water Utilities; no recorded City easements cross either parcel per City easement layer. Main sizes/capacity need availability request + capacity application.
electric: Lakeland Electric (municipal) service territory. New service starts with LE Energy Delivery Engineering's Commercial Project Application (site + electrical CAD, load data); CIAC may apply; downtown service is typically underground. Economic Development Riders (EDIR-1: 350 kW+ and 25+ new FTEs, 25%->5% discount over 5 yrs; EDIR-2 smaller loads) fit office/commercial users, not apartments. System context: record 792 MW peak (Feb 2026); OUC power-purchase deal extended through 12/31/2027. No public feeder/substation capacity data; ask LE.
fiber: City-owned fiber network (~330-350 mi) commercialized by Summit Broadband; downtown in service area. Building-level availability not published; ask Summit/City.
stormwater: Lot is already almost entirely paved, so a building generally does not add impervious area, but redevelopment still needs City Public Works stormwater review and likely a SWFWMD Environmental Resource Permit (new statewide stormwater rule in effect since 2024). Downtown projects usually use underground vaults; CRA reimbursed underground stormwater for Peachtree Flats. City stormwater utility fee applies to impervious area. Near Lake Mirror, so discharge/treatment standards for the lake may matter.

Live Local Act path (F.S. 166.04151(7)): with 40% of units affordable (<=120% AMI) for 30 yrs, City must allow height up to the tallest allowed within 1 mile (C-6 = 120 ft nearby), FAR up to 7.5 (150% of 5.0), administrative approval; density stays capped at 175 du/ac, so it adds height/flexibility, not units.
open_questions: Board/owner appetite (LEDC-affiliated owner). FDEP ACTIVE petroleum cleanup at Firestone #1946, 202 N Massachusetts Ave (remedial action underway, status updated Oct 2025) on or right next to the lot, so get a Phase I/II and ask FDEP about plume extent. Flood elevation. Utility capacity calls.

loading_bike: Loading (LDC 4.11.7): uses receiving deliveries need 10x25 / 10x50 ft off-street spaces; commercial retail 0-4,999 sf = one 10x25; 5,000-19,999 sf = one 10x50; 20,000-49,999 sf = two 10x50. live_local: F.S. 166.04151(7) (Live Local): multifamily/mixed-use must be allowed on commercial land if 40% of rental units are affordable (<=120% AMI) for 30 years. City may not cap density below the highest allowed anywhere in the city (175 du/ac downtown, so no gain here), FAR below 150% of the highest allowed (5.0 -> 7.5; FAR includes lot coverage), or height below the tallest allowed within 1 mile (C-6 = 120 ft). Must be approved administratively, without board action, if it meets the multifamily LDRs other than density/FAR/height/use. The historic-district carve-outs ((7)(d)3 height and (7)(e)3 design) apply only to parcels WITH a contributing structure in a district NR-listed before 2000 (Munn Park NR-listed 1997); this lot is a surface lot, so they appear not to apply. Confirm with City Planning and the City Attorney. Mixed-use projects must be at least 65% residential by floor area. Affordable-housing incentives (City 2026 Local Housing Incentives Review): concept and site plan review expedited to 10 days instead of 30; non-utility City impact fees waived/reimbursed inside the Central City Transit Supportive Area based on income.
parking_outlook: Inside the Downtown Parking Exempt Area (LDC 4.11.2). LDC26-005 (P&Z final decision Nov 17, 2026) redraws Figure 4.11-1 for readability; the new map still shows this lot inside. Any parking that is built must meet the LDC design and landscaping standards. Note: the lot is the Terrace Hotel's parking today.
sewer_water_context: Downtown CRA Plan Update draft (Aug 20, 2026): sewer transmission is 'the most critical infrastructure variable'. Western Trunk ($25M, 42-in PVC) is finishing and serves Downtown West/Lake Wire; Eastern Trunk Phase 1 ($45M, bond-funded) is programmed in the FY2026 CIP, and until it is done large vertical projects in the East Main Street district are constrained. Historic-core storefronts are often on 4-inch water lines that can't support fire flow; the City requires service/fire-line size and fire-flow documentation in commercial water plan review. Which trunk serves this lot needs a Water Utilities call.
planning_questions: Live Local carve-outs for a vacant lot inside Munn Park district; 30,000 sf max lot-area rule when combining 2 parcels; easement relocation (City Commission); which sewer trunk serves the lot.

cra: Downtown CRA. Precedents: Peachtree Flats TIF rebate = 75% of City+County increment for 5 yrs after CO, plus up to $775k site/infrastructure reimbursement; Onicx (Oak St, 2022) = 80% yrs 1-5 / 60% yrs 6-10 plus fee help. LDDA Curb Appeal grant (50% match) for storefront items.

water_sewer: City of Lakeland Water Utilities serves downtown. No public main-size map (City GeoHub publishes easements only); no recorded City utility easements cross this parcel. Main sizes/capacity need an availability request + Water & Wastewater Capacity application.
electric: Lakeland Electric (municipal) service territory. New service starts with LE Energy Delivery Engineering's Commercial Project Application (site + electrical CAD, load data); CIAC may apply; downtown service is typically underground. Economic Development Riders (EDIR-1: 350 kW+ and 25+ new FTEs, 25%->5% discount over 5 yrs; EDIR-2 smaller loads) fit office/commercial users, not apartments. System context: record 792 MW peak (Feb 2026); OUC power-purchase deal extended through 12/31/2027. No public feeder/substation capacity data; ask LE.
fiber: City-owned fiber network (~330-350 mi) commercialized by Summit Broadband; downtown in service area. Building-level availability not published; ask Summit/City.
stormwater: Lot is already almost entirely paved, so a building generally does not add impervious area, but redevelopment still needs City Public Works stormwater review and likely a SWFWMD Environmental Resource Permit (new statewide stormwater rule in effect since 2024). Downtown projects usually use underground vaults; CRA reimbursed underground stormwater for Peachtree Flats. City stormwater utility fee applies to impervious area.
